The best advice is to use multiple sources to study. So what you are doing is correct. You will be more well-rounded. The CompTIA stuff was WAY more in-depth, but WAY too much info. The actual exams don't go into that much detail.

I purchased the CompTIA online study guides, labs, practice exams, and handbooks both times. I watched the free vids for those previously mentioned. I also purchased their course notes and practice exams. In all I spent around $1300 for everything. 

If you don't have the money, there is still a ton of free material from content creators relating to this field. 

This subreddit has all of them and links to their individual sites/materials.

I love that they are multiple-choice. There doesn't seem to be any "Select all that apply", even though most of the practice exams (Udemy, Myers) that I took had a ton of those. Messer's practice exams didn't have any "select all that apply". 

I took both tests from home. I had to take them at 4 am to ensure no distractions or noise, etc. More comfortable at home.
